capabilities.title: Typed, validated catalogs and English interface catalog
capabilities.contract: English is the only complete installed catalog. Application copy is catalog-validated, production surfaces inherit the root locale provider, and localized text is excluded from selectors and logic.
capabilities.persistence: Localized defaults become Article data only when author-editable content is created.

capabilities.title: Semantic controls, focus treatment, keyboard navigation, and non-color cues
capabilities.contract: Workspace and Settings controls expose semantic labels, keyboard access, visible focus, and non-color status conventions.
capabilities.persistence: Accessibility behavior is derived from rendered controls and does not persist sensitive state.

capabilities.title: Shortcut hints, normalization, conflict detection, and command registration
capabilities.contract: Key bindings normalize, resolve defaults, identify conflicts, and register commands.
capabilities.persistence: Author-selected overrides persist in Application Settings.
limitations: Complete workspace-action wiring remains follow-up work.

capabilities.title: Shared success and error provider with viewport
capabilities.contract: Recoverable failures are presented through a shared notification API without exposing sensitive values.

capabilities.title: Shared contracts, HTTP constants, and transport-boundary validation
capabilities.contract: Shared validation and HTTP constants reject malformed transport data before it reaches application behavior.
capabilities.persistence: Invalid provider or transport payloads are not persisted as valid application data.

capabilities.title: Server-side secrets, local materials, minimal context, redacted diagnostics, and storage opt-in
capabilities.contract: Secrets remain server-side, including custom-named values loaded from the project .env file before local-service startup; materials remain local, only necessary request context is sent, and provider response storage requires explicit opt-in.
capabilities.persistence: Private content is not logged or traced by default; provider-side response storage is disabled unless enabled.

capabilities.title: SQLite persistence and Article schema transition
capabilities.contract: Startup performs the one-time legacy Documents-to-Articles schema transition, then preserves the resulting Article database.
capabilities.persistence: SQLite remains the durable local data store after migration.

capabilities.title: Local Article conversation records
capabilities.contract: Greetings, messages, request scope, completions, and safe failure or cancellation status are isolated per Article; author messages retain resolved skills and offsets.
capabilities.persistence: Conversation records are local and cascade with their Article; fixed application messages use stable templates while author and model content remain authored text.

capabilities.title: Persistent application-level checkpoint, Revision, backup, and future sync activity
capabilities.contract: A future activity center is distinct from popup-notification history and does not replace contextual recovery.
capabilities.persistence: Deferred until the post-MVP design and storage contract are approved.

capabilities.title: Accounts, sync, teams, analytics, direct publishing, imports, exports, additional providers, and alternate clients
capabilities.contract: These capabilities remain outside the validated MVP editorial loop.
capabilities.persistence: No persistence or network surface is introduced for deferred MVP work.

scenarios.title: Installed interface catalogs must be complete
preconditions: A locale catalog is registered for the application.
expected: The complete English catalog validates and is the only installed catalog.

scenarios.title: Workspace layout controls remain accessible
scenarios.event: The author navigates or resizes workspace panels.
expected: Panel controls expose accessible labels and semantic separators.
forbidden: Panel behavior is not conveyed by color alone.

scenarios.title: Key bindings normalize and detect conflicts
preconditions: Default bindings and an author override are available.
scenarios.event: The binding resolver normalizes and compares key chords.
expected: Defaults, explicit unassignment, and duplicate chords are resolved deterministically.
forbidden: Conflicting effective chords are not silently accepted.

scenarios.title: Notification errors remain recoverable and redacted
preconditions: An application client error or unknown exception occurs.
scenarios.event: The notification provider presents the failure.
expected: A useful localized failure notification is shown.
forbidden: Private diagnostic detail is not displayed.

scenarios.title: Malformed health transport data is rejected
preconditions: A health response is received from the local service.
scenarios.event: The shared contract validates the response.
expected: Valid health data is accepted and malformed data is rejected.
forbidden: Malformed transport data does not become application state.

scenarios.title: Provider response storage remains opt-in
preconditions: Server configuration is loaded with or without storage settings.
scenarios.event: The configuration parser resolves privacy settings.
expected: Provider response storage is disabled by default and tracing is rejected.
forbidden: Ambiguous storage values or remote tracing are not enabled.

scenarios.title: Database transition preserves the resulting Article database
preconditions: A legacy Documents database exists before local service startup.
scenarios.event: The service starts for the first time after the Article migration.
expected: The legacy database and sidecars are replaced once with the Article schema.
forbidden: Future starts do not delete the resulting Article database.

scenarios.title: Assistant conversation records remain isolated per Article
preconditions: An Article has an Assistant greeting and author request.
expected: Greeting templates and resolved author skill metadata remain available for the Article.
forbidden: Conversation state does not cross Article boundaries.

scenarios.title: Data-protection activity center is explicitly deferred
scenarios.event: A change proposes persistent activity-center work.
expected: The work is tracked as post-MVP rather than inferred into current scope.
forbidden: Popup notification history is not treated as the activity center.

scenarios.title: Deferred MVP capabilities remain out of scope
scenarios.event: An MVP implementation change is planned.
expected: The capability remains deferred unless the active issue explicitly changes scope.
forbidden: Deferred product surface is not silently introduced.
